name: Resisted Hip Flexion
family: Hip flexion and leg raise (standing cable)
tierNote: Safety tier C (content.md 5.1: not in the A or B lists); census.json difficulty tier 1.

claims.text: Attach an ankle strap to a low cable pulley around one ankle; stand facing away from the machine with slight cable tension, holding something stable for balance if needed.

quotes.text: Attach ankle strap to low cable pulley and secure around one ankle. Stand facing away from machine with slight cable tension, holding stable object for balance if needed.

claims.text: Face away from the machine holding the frame, drive the knee up and forward against the cable until the thigh nears hip height, lower with control, then switch legs.

quotes.text: Face away from the machine and hold the frame for balance. Drive your knee up and forward against the cable, lifting your thigh toward hip height, then lower with control and repeat before switching legs.

claims.text: Brace the core and stay upright; lift the strapped leg forward slowly, bending the knee toward the chest, and pause briefly at the top.

quotes.text: Brace core and maintain upright posture.
Slowly lift strapped leg forward, bending knee toward chest.
Pause briefly at top to squeeze hip flexors.

claims.text: Lower the leg back with control, without letting the weight stack touch down or drop.

quotes.text: Controlled lower leg back to start without letting weight stack touch.
Control the cable back down rather than letting it drop

claims.text: Range: from the hip fully extended behind the body to the thigh parallel to the floor or the knee near the chest, without arching the lower back.

quotes.text: From full hip extension behind body to thigh parallel to floor or knee near chest, without lumbar arch.

claims.text: Core tight with no arching; lift with the hip, not momentum; hips level and square with no rotation; knee tracks straight.

quotes.text: Core tight, no arching.
Lift with hip, not momentum.
Hips level, no rotation.
Knee tracks straight.
Keep hips square throughout.

claims.text: Mistakes: leaning back or arching the lower back to lift higher, swinging the leg up, and letting the stack slam at the bottom.

quotes.text: Don't lean back or arch your lower back to lift higher
Don't swing the leg up with momentum
Don't let the stack slam at the bottom

claims.text: Tempo 2-1-2; breathe in while lowering, out while lifting.

quotes.text: Inhale during lowering phase; exhale as you lift and squeeze.
Tempo 2-1-2

claims.text: Typical sets: 10-15 reps with 60-90 seconds rest.

quotes.text: Typical Rep Range 10-15 reps Rest Between Sets 60-90 seconds

claims.text: It mainly works the hip flexors (iliopsoas), with the quads (rectus femoris) and the abs assisting.

quotes.text: The cable standing hip flexion mainly works the hip flexors, with the lower abs, quads, and upper abs assisting.
Hip Flexors10/10 Iliopsoas Quads7/10 Rectus Femoris

claims.text: Avoid it with acute hip or low-back pain; start light to learn the form; keep a neutral spine; stop if balancing causes strain.

quotes.text: Avoid if acute hip or low back pain present.
Use light weight initially for form.
Maintain neutral spine to protect lower back.
Stop if balance causes strain.

claims.text: Feel the front of the hip and the lower abs pull the knee up; stand tall with the standing leg steady.

quotes.text: Feel the front of your hip and lower abs pull your knee up
Stand tall and keep your standing leg steady

claims.text: Band version: loop a long band round a low anchor and round the top of the shoe; stand upright facing away from the anchor, far enough to put tension on the band.

quotes.text: Secure a resistance band with a long loop around a low anchor point. Place the other end of the band around the top of your shoe.
Stand upright with good posture, facing away from the anchor point of the band. Make sure to stand far enough away to create tension in the band.

claims.text: With the core and glutes tight, drive the knee up toward the chest; hold a wall for support if balance needs it.

quotes.text: Keeping your core and glutes tight, drive your knee up to your chest, squeezing your hip flexors.
You can also opt to hold onto something, such as a wall, for support.

claims.text: Hold at the top for 2-3 seconds, then lower slowly, resisting the pull.

quotes.text: Hold and squeeze at the top position for 2-3 seconds. Slowly lower your leg back down, resisting the pull of the band by contracting your hip flexors.

claims.text: 10 to 15 reps a leg; progress to a band with more tension; hold a wall or table if balance is hard.

quotes.text: Perform 10 to 15 reps before switching legs.
Over time, you can replace the current resistance band with one of greater tension. If you have trouble balancing, hold onto a wall or table for support.

claims.text: The main hip flexors are the psoas major and iliacus (iliopsoas); the rectus femoris, a quad muscle, also flexes the hip.

quotes.text: The primary muscles in your hip flexors are the psoas major and the iliacus. Together, these muscles are referred to as the iliopsoas. Other important muscles in this group include the rectus femoris (one of your quad muscles), the sartorius, and the pectineus.

sources.title: Cable Standing Hip Flexor Raise: Exercise Guide (Motra)
Cable Standing Hip Flexion: How to Do It, Form & Muscles Worked (Kovo)
9 Hip Flexor Exercises to Improve Your Athletic Performance (Outside, Amber Sayer, certified personal trainer)

plate.viewWhy: The thigh rising to parallel (c2, c5), the upright torso (c3) and the lean-back fault (c7) are sagittal.
plate.equipment: Cable column with a low pulley and an ankle cuff on the working ankle (census needs cable, ankleCuff); the cable runs back from the ankle to the pulley behind the lifter; one hand on the frame (c1, c2). Floor line.
plate.frames: Rep convention: start with the strapped leg slightly behind the body, end with the thigh about parallel to the floor; Trace follows the knee.
plate.start: Standing tall, facing away from the column, slight cable tension, hand on the frame (c1, c2); strapped hip extended behind the body (c5); core braced (c3).
plate.end: Strapped thigh about parallel to the floor, knee bent (c2, c3, c5); torso still upright, hips level (c3, c6); standing leg steady (c12).

checkpoints.label: Stand tall
checkpoints.what: Upright, core braced, standing leg steady.

checkpoints.label: Thigh to hip height
checkpoints.what: Knee drives up and forward until the thigh is about parallel.

checkpoints.label: No back arch
checkpoints.what: Core tight; don't lean back to lift higher.

mistake.what: Leaning back and arching the lower back to lift the knee higher.
mistake.why: Kovo lists it first among mistakes (c7); Motra's range stops short of a lumbar arch (c5).

tempo.text: Motra gives 2-1-2 (c8, WEAK); the named band source holds 2-3 s at the top and lowers slowly (c15). Drawn: 2 s up, 2 s hold, 2 s down.

plate.variantLine: The library lists cable or resistance band. The plate draws the cable with an ankle cuff (census). The band version (band round a low anchor and the shoe, facing away) is sourced separately (c13-c16). Each shown line cites the claims for the version it describes; the cable-only claims are WEAK.

grip.type: One hand holds the machine frame for balance (c1, c2).

setup.step: Strap the cuff to one ankle on a low cable, or loop a band round a low anchor and your shoe.
Face away from the anchor with a little tension; hold the frame or a wall.
Brace your core and stand tall.
Drive the knee up and forward until your thigh is about level.
Hold briefly, then lower slowly and switch legs after the set.

handlingMistakes.fix: Stand tall and stop at thigh level.

rows.means: Your hip flexors lift the knee.
Your abs help pull the knee up.
You're leaning back or arching to lift higher.
rows.fix: Stand tall, core tight, lighter weight.

risks.risk: Arching the lower back to lift higher.
Sudden, recent hip or lower-back pain: skip this exercise.
Balancing on one leg can strain; stop if it does.

zooms.right: Torso upright, thigh at hip height.
zooms.wrong: Torso leaning back, lower back arched.

zooms.right: Cuff around the ankle, cable taut behind you.

libraryDiff.why: Library: hip_flexors primary; quads secondary; core stabiliser. Motra and Kovo name the hip flexors first, then the quads (rectus femoris) and the abs (c10). Matches; no change.

anchorNote: R-W0-2: Amber Sayer's Outside article (a named certified personal trainer; byline in the page metadata) read in full; its "Resisted Hip Hikes" is this exercise with a band anchored low, facing away (c13-c16). Motra and Kovo (cable, read in full) are app exercise-database pages that name no author, so every claim resting only on them is tagged WEAK. No ACE, NASM or PubMed technique source was found. Also read, not cited: The Prehab Guys (straight-knee kick, a different movement) and Wellen (loop band round both ankles, a marching variant; no named author).

loadProgression.text: Start light; sets of 10-15 reps a leg; move to a band with more tension as you get stronger.

unsourced: Straight-leg vs bent-knee version: both sources bend the knee; a straight-leg band raise exists but was not read.
notes: Range conflict: Kovo lifts the thigh toward hip height (c2); Motra allows up to the knee near the chest (c3, c5). The plate draws the thigh about parallel, which both allow.
The lower-back row links redFlag 'back' as a pending link (LR-11, LR-27, LR-28); the sheet cannot ship before the back-pain box.

Fix round 2026-10-02 (verify w0): A7/R-W0-2: claims resting only on motra-hf or kovo-hf tagged WEAK; a named source (Outside, Amber Sayer, CPT) added as anchor with c13-c17; setup and tempo now cite it; variantLine rewritten so it does not say the two versions share rules. The anchor is a band source while the plate draws the cable. Supervisor ruling R-W0-7 (2026-10-02, verify/w0.md): the bar is met. The movement is the same (low anchor behind, facing away, knee drive, hold, slow lower), and content.md 3.2 asks for an exercise-specific technique source. The cable-only setup stays on the WEAK full-access pages, and the plate draws nothing that only the band source gives.
Recheck Low 1 (2026-10-02): loadProgression no longer says "more weight", which no cited claim supports; it follows c16 (a band with greater tension).
